NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION) — Intervention: Schedule aeration-induced relaxation with sub-atmospheric air pulses between backwashes to disrupt compact biofilm layers. Standard practice: Backwash every 30 min with no chemical or aeration modulation. Mitigation: Introduce timed, brief sub-atmospheric air pulses during relaxation to create localized shear stress that disrupts biofilm cohesion. Adjacent-technique clearance: Closest practice is constant aeration during operation; departure is pulsed sub-atmospheric air during relaxation, exploiting pressure differentials for shear. Mechanism: Pulsed vacuum shear disrupts biofilm adhesion before consolidation.

PHYSICS CHECK — Governing relation: Biofilm consolidation rate ∝ (adhesion strength × compressive stress). Intervention reduces adhesion strength by inducing shear stress via pressure differentials (ΔP = -0.2 bar for 5 sec), disrupting extracellular polymeric substance (EPS) bonds. Magnitude: Shear stress τ = ΔP/d (d = fibre spacing ≈ 1 mm) → τ ≈ 20 Pa, exceeding biofilm yield strength (≈5–10 Pa), causing fragmentation.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL —  
1. Standard backwash valve (a)  
2. Standard aeration blower (a)  
3. Standard pressure sensor (a)  
4. Standard timer/controller (a)  
5. Commercial solenoid valve, DN25, 3-way (b)  
6. Commercial vacuum regulator, 0–-0.5 bar range (b)  
7. Commercial EPDM gasket, DN25 (b)  
8. Procedure: Set timer to trigger vacuum valve for 5 sec every 15 min during relaxation (c)  

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY) —  
- Installation: Standard valve (a) + standard blower (a) + standard sensor (a) + standard controller (a) + catalog solenoid valve (b) + catalog vacuum regulator (b) + catalog gasket (b) → same as standard practice (valve/blower/sensor/controller).  
- Commissioning: Parameter programming (c) only, no new tooling.  
- Operation: Vacuum pulses use existing blower capacity; energy cost <1% of aeration power (negligible).  
- Maintenance: Catalog parts match standard practice’s maintenance class.  
- Operational cost: Zero (pulses scheduled during non-production relaxation windows).  

EXECUTABLE TEST — Protocol: Run 3 modules with intervention vs. 3 controls at 20 LMH; measure irreversible flux decline after 30 days. Instruments: Flux meters, pressure sensors. Pass/fail: Intervention group shows ≥30% lower irreversible flux decline (p<0.05, ANOVA). Kill criterion: Flux decline >10% in any module within 7 days. Duration: 30 days.  

MECHANISM CLASS: Aeration-pulsed relaxation disruption  
CANDIDATE CLASSES:  
- Chemical antifoulant dosing — disrupts EPS biochemistry  
- Flux setpoint reduction — lowers compressive stress  
- Aeration-pulsed relaxation disruption — induces shear stress via pressure pulses  
SELECTED: Aeration-pulsed relaxation disruption (non-duty-cycle; chemical dosing excluded by constraint, flux reduction sacrifices throughput).  

SIGNALS USED: None (open-loop timer-driven).  
DIRECTION-OF-EFFECT: Driving variable = biofilm adhesion strength; mechanism moves it down by shear stress from pressure pulses; this reduces the failure driver (consolidation rate).  
OPERATIONAL COST: Zero (pulses during relaxation, no production impact).
